extra.message: USERS_XML embeds hardcoded plaintext user credentials (e.g. admin password '7en8aiDoh!') directly in source code. Anyone with read access to the repository obtains valid credentials, and the same secrets are also stored in the database.

User-controlled query parameter params['id'] is concatenated directly into the SQL string passed to cursor.execute() ('SELECT ... WHERE id=' + params['id']) with no sanitization or parameter binding. This allows boolean, time-based, and UNION-based SQL injection to read or modify arbitrary data (e.g. dump user passwords).

User-controlled query parameter params['v'] is inserted unescaped into HTML_POSTFIX via re.sub and returned in the HTML response body. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript, resulting in reflected XSS.
User-controlled query parameter params['object'] is passed to pickle.loads(). Deserializing attacker-supplied pickle data allows arbitrary code execution on the server.

User-controlled query parameter params['path'] is passed to open(os.path.abspath(...)) with no allowlist or canonicalization check. os.path.abspath does not prevent traversal, so values like '/etc/passwd' or '../../secret' let a remote attacker read arbitrary files on the server.

When params['path'] contains '://', it is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen() and the response body is returned to the requester. An attacker can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs (including file:// and internal network addresses), enabling server-side request forgery.

User-controlled query parameter params['domain'] is concatenated into a shell command string and executed via subprocess.run(..., shell=True). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; cat /etc/passwd') to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

User-controlled XML in params['xml'] is parsed with lxml.etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). External entities are resolved and network fetches allowed, enabling XML External Entity (XXE) attacks to read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service (billion laughs).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User-controlled query parameter params['name'] is interpolated via '%s' into an XPath expression passed to lxml .xpath(). An attacker can alter the query (e.g. '] | //user/password/text() | //user[name/text()[\'') to extract arbitrary data from USERS_XML, including passwords.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: User-controlled params['size'] is converted with int() and used to build a string of size N x N ('#' * N repeated N times) with no upper bound. A single request with a large size value (e.g. 100000000) exhausts server memory/CPU, causing denial of service.

cwe: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: User-controlled query parameter params['comment'] is interpolated via '%s' directly into an INSERT statement executed by cursor.execute() with no escaping or parameter binding. This allows SQL injection through the comment parameter (and the inserted payload is later rendered, compounding into stored XSS).

Comment text stored in the database (originating from the unvalidated 'comment' parameter at line 50) is rendered into HTML table cells without any escaping. An attacker can store a malicious script via a comment, which executes in the browser of every user who views /?comment= (stored XSS).

User-controlled params['include'] is read from a local file path (open) or remote URL (urllib.request.urlopen) and the resulting bytes are executed with exec(program, envs). This allows an attacker to execute arbitrary Python code from a local file or a remote server (local/remote file inclusion leading to remote code execution).

cwe: CWE-98: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program ('PHP Remote File Inclusion')

extra.message: exec(program, envs) executes content fully derived from the user-controlled 'include' parameter. Combined with the unvalidated file/URL read on line 56, this is a direct remote code execution sink (dynamic code evaluation of untrusted input).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: When params['include'] contains '://', it is passed to urllib.request.urlopen(), causing the server to fetch an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL. This is a server-side request forgery vector (in addition to the file-inclusion/exec impact).

User-controlled params['redir'] is placed unvalidated into a <meta http-equiv='refresh' content='0; url=...'> tag, causing the browser to redirect to an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL. This is an open redirect usable for phishing; the unescaped value is also injectable into the HTML head.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: User-controlled params['callback'] is concatenated verbatim around the JSON response of /users.json without validating that it is a legitimate JavaScript identifier. An attacker can supply arbitrary JavaScript as the callback, producing reflected XSS when the endpoint is loaded in a browser (JSONP callback injection).

The login query concatenates params['password'] directly into the SQL string (only 'username' is filtered). A payload such as password=' OR '1' LIKE '1 authenticates as any user without a valid password, giving SQL-injection-based authentication bypass.

The SESSIONID cookie is set via a <meta http-equiv='Set-Cookie'> tag with only 'path=/' — no HttpOnly and no Secure attributes. The session token is readable by any injected JavaScript (combining with the app's XSS flaws) and can be transmitted over plaintext HTTP.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: On any unhandled exception the handler returns traceback.format_exc() (or subprocess ex.output) to the remote client with a 500 response. Full stack traces disclose internal paths, code, SQL fragments, and runtime details useful to an attacker.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The server explicitly sends 'X-XSS-Protection: 0' on every response, disabling the browser's built-in reflected-XSS filter. This weakens client-side defenses against the multiple XSS vulnerabilities present in the application.

User-controlled params['charset'] is placed unvalidated into the Content-Type response header value via send_header(). Since the value is URL-decoded and not checked for CR/LF, an attacker can inject newline characters to split the response and inject arbitrary HTTP headers or body content (HTTP response splitting).

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting')

extra.message: The Dockerfile rewrites LISTEN_ADDRESS from 127.0.0.1 to 0.0.0.0 and exposes port 65412, binding this deliberately vulnerable application (SQLi, RCE via exec/pickle, LFI, etc.) to all network interfaces inside the container. Anyone who can reach the published port gains remote code execution.
